title: Per-household evacuation behaviour: evidence and profiles for sim/behavior.py draw_household_choices
units: probabilities and weights are fractions; times are minutes; hours are local clock hours 0-24

labels.sourced: value read from the cited document (page or table in `locator`)
labels.derived: arithmetic on sourced values, shown in `derivation`
labels.assumption: no source gives it; a placeholder for sensitivity runs, not a finding
labels.legacy: reproduces the model's behaviour before this file (no evidence claimed)
labels.gap: looked for and not found; nothing in the model uses it

transferability_scale: high: same kind of event and population (fast California WUI fire); medium: other US wildfire or a different warning regime; low: stated intentions, another country's policy, another hazard, or a qualitative count
page_convention: Wong et al. 2020, Grajdura 2022 and NIST TN 2252: printed page numbers. NIST TN 2103: PDF page (printed = PDF - 5). Forrister et al. 2024 and Kuligowski et al. 2022: PDF pages of the versions in `url`.

sources.wong2020: Wong, S.D., Broader, J.C., Shaheen, S.A. (2020). Review of California Wildfire Evacuations from 2017 to 2019. UC ITS report, DOI 10.7922/G29G5K2R. https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5w85z07g. Online surveys: Oct 2017 N. California (Tubbs, Nuns, Atlas) n=79; Dec 2017 S. California (Thomas, Creek, Skirball) n=226; Carr 2018 n=284.
sources.wong2023: Wong, S.D., Broader, J.C., Walker, J.L., Shaheen, S.A. (2023). Understanding California wildfire evacuee behavior and joint choice making. Transportation 50:1165-1211, DOI 10.1007/s11116-022-10275-y. Pre-print read: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4fm7d34j (same survey data as wong2020).
sources.grajdura2022: Grajdura, S. (2022). Mixed Methods Approaches to Wildfire Evacuation: Modeling Behavior, Simulation, and Equity. PhD dissertation, UC Davis. https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3t8025w5. Camp Fire survey n=397 (133 shelter, 264 online), 26 shelter interviews.
sources.nist2252: Maranghides, A., et al. (2023). A Case Study of the Camp Fire: Notification, Evacuation, Traffic, and Temporary Refuge Areas. NIST TN 2252, DOI 10.6028/NIST.TN.2252. Reconstruction from 911, radio, video and interviews; no resident survey.
sources.nist2252sup: NIST TN 2252 Supplement (2023), Appendix D Tables D-2, D-3 (CodeRED delivery), parsed in tools/comms_fixtures/codered_delivery_table.json and summarised in tools/comms_degradation.json `alerting`.
sources.zhao2022: Zhao, X., Xu, Y., Lovreglio, R., Kuligowski, E., et al. (2022). Estimating wildfire evacuation decision and departure timing using large-scale GPS data. Transportation Research Part D. arXiv:2109.07745. Kincade 2019, 5,166 inferred homes.
sources.kuligowski2022: Kuligowski, E.D., Zhao, X., Lovreglio, R., et al. (2022). Modeling evacuation decisions in the 2019 Kincade fire in California. Safety Science 146. Author manuscript https://mro.massey.ac.nz/bitstreams/be2703da-d4ac-4ca5-97d8-7a0a04f99e16/download. Online survey n=270.
sources.sun2024: Sun, Y., Forrister, A., Kuligowski, E.D., Lovreglio, R., Cova, T.J., Zhao, X. (2024). Social vulnerabilities and wildfire evacuations: a case study of the 2019 Kincade Fire. Safety Science. arXiv:2402.06639. GPS, 135 block groups.
sources.forrister2024: Forrister, A., Kuligowski, E.D., Sun, Y., Yan, X., Lovreglio, R., Cova, T.J., Zhao, X. (2024). Analyzing risk perception, evacuation decision and delay time: a case study of the 2021 Marshall Fire in Colorado. Travel Behaviour and Society 35:100729. Online survey N=191.
sources.forrister2022qr: Forrister, A., et al. (2022). Marshall Fire quick response report, Natural Hazards Center QR 349 (HTML), Table 1 'Transportation Decisions Made by Evacuees', N=132 evacuees.
sources.walpole2020: Walpole, E.H., Kuligowski, E.D., et al. (2020). NIST TN 2103 (Chimney Tops 2 fire, Gatlinburg TN, 2016, household survey), DOI 10.6028/NIST.TN.2103. N=323 (280 evacuees, 43 stayed).
sources.lovreglio2020: Lovreglio, R., Kuligowski, E., Walpole, E., Link, E., Gwynne, S. (2020). Calibrating the Wildfire Decision Model using hybrid choice modelling. IJDRR 50:101770 (Chimney Tops 2 data). Massey author manuscript.
sources.mclennan2014: McLennan, J., Elliott, G., Wright, L. (2014). Bushfire survival preparations by householders in at-risk areas of south-eastern Australia. Australian Journal of Emergency Management 29(2). n=584, hypothetical scenario.
sources.people_behavior: tools/people_behavior.json (this repository): earlier sourced parameters, same evidence rule.
sources.mclennan2019: McLennan, J., Ryan, B., Bearman, C., Toh, K. (2019). Should we leave now? Behavioral factors in evacuation under wildfire threat. Fire Technology 55:487-516. Read: USQ author preprint (manuscript pages, not mapped to journal pages). Review of eight Australian field-interview studies (23 fires, n=1,641) and surveys.
sources.whittaker2021: Whittaker, J., et al. (2021). Black Summer: how the NSW community responded to the 2019-20 bushfire season. Bushfire and Natural Hazards CRC Report 651. Survey n=1,004 (773 residents) and 202 interviews.
sources.mcgee2018: McGee, T.K. (2018). Residents' experiences of the 2016 Fort McMurray Wildfire, Alberta. In Viegas (Ed.), Advances in Forest Fire Research 2018, pp. 1155-1159. Online survey n=447 (self-selected, 81% women).
sources.cfa2020: CFA / BNHCRC (2020). Application of Self-Evacuation Archetypes (Safer Together), Table 6 p. 48, reporting Strahan, Whittaker and Handmer (2018) IJDRR 27:307-316 archetype shares (the 2018 paper itself was not read).

order_compliance_wong.population: survey respondents who received a mandatory order
order_compliance_wong.label: sourced
order_compliance_wong.transferability: high for Oct 2017 N. California (fast, wind-driven, night, low notice; the analogue choice is ours); convenience sample

evacuation_rate_other_fires.behaviour: Respondents who evacuated (all respondents, ordered or not)
evacuation_rate_other_fires.locator: Kuligowski 2022 p. 12; Forrister 2024 Table 4 p. 8; TN 2103 PDF pp. 29, 42
evacuation_rate_other_fires.label: sourced
evacuation_rate_other_fires.transferability: medium: corroborates that 13% to 31% do not leave; not used as a parameter

shadow_evacuation_wong.behaviour: Non-recipients of an order who evacuated
shadow_evacuation_wong.label: sourced
shadow_evacuation_wong.transferability: medium: small cells; Carr had a 2-day build-up

stay_reasons_gatlinburg.behaviour: Reasons for staying (select all), people who stayed
stay_reasons_gatlinburg.label: sourced
stay_reasons_gatlinburg.transferability: medium: night, no-notice, almost no official warning (83% received none); like Camp

stay_reasons_wong.behaviour: Non-evacuees who wanted to protect property (select all)
stay_reasons_wong.locator: Table 20, p. 51 (also: did not receive any orders 71.4/47.1/30.0%; did not want to leave 31.0/39.2/26.7%; went back home due to traffic 0.0/2.0/3.3%)
stay_reasons_wong.label: sourced

camp_fatalities_by_activity.locator: p. 218 (deaths), p. 193 (refusals), p. 217 (at least 42% of victims had a mobility or medical condition)
camp_fatalities_by_activity.label: sourced
camp_fatalities_by_activity.transferability: high (outcome check, not a behaviour share)

camp_temporary_refuge.behaviour: Civilians who sheltered at temporary refuge areas (TRAs) instead of driving out

value.share_of_paradise_population: 5% to 9% at 1.0 person per vehicle, 12% at 2.5

camp_temporary_refuge.label: sourced
camp_temporary_refuge.transferability: high for Camp; TRAs are an outcome of blocked roads, not a home decision; the traffic twin models refuges separately

wait_and_see_intent_mclennan.behaviour: Stated plan if a fire would reach the home in 1-2 h: leave at once / stay and defend / wait and see
wait_and_see_intent_mclennan.label: sourced
wait_and_see_intent_mclennan.transferability: low: stated intention to a hypothetical under the Australian stay-or-go policy; kept as the high sensitivity value (0.29 of all respondents, 0.33 of compliers)

wait_and_see_states_lovreglio.behaviour: Wildfire Decision Model states (no reaction, investigate, vigilant, respond)
wait_and_see_states_lovreglio.locator: Table 3 PDF p. 20; Sec. 3.6 worked example (a model prediction, not a sample share)
wait_and_see_states_lovreglio.label: sourced
wait_and_see_states_lovreglio.transferability: medium: Chimney Tops 2 data; would need the latent risk model to use

camp_first_awareness.behaviour: How Camp respondents first found out about the fire
camp_first_awareness.label: sourced
camp_first_awareness.transferability: high for a no-notice fire; low for fires with hours of official notice (Kincade: 73% received an order)

camp_order_received.behaviour: Camp respondents who received an evacuation order at any time on 8 Nov 2018
camp_order_received.label: sourced

official_order_received_other.behaviour: Respondents who received an official order or warning
official_order_received_other.locator: Kuligowski 2022 p. 11; Forrister 2024 Table 4 p. 8 and p. 7; TN 2103 PDF pp. 19-22; Wong 2020 Table 12 p. 40
official_order_received_other.label: sourced
official_order_received_other.transferability: medium: use for a scenario with notice

official_channels_kincade.label: sourced
official_channels_kincade.transferability: medium (Sonoma County after Tubbs; WEA share not reported)

official_channels_wong.behaviour: Channels by which mandatory-order recipients got the order (select all), Oct 2017 N. California / Dec 2017 S. California / Carr
official_channels_wong.label: sourced

camp_codered_delivery.locator: pp. 43-44, Table 8; p. xxiii and p. 42 (no IPAWS/WEA)
camp_codered_delivery.label: sourced
camp_codered_delivery.transferability: high for Camp; registration and dial capacity vary by county

codered_success_by_hour.behaviour: CodeRED initial-call connect share by message time, Camp 8-9 Nov 2018
codered_success_by_hour.label: derived
codered_success_by_hour.transferability: low for the hour effect: the after-midnight calls (580 contacts) went to remote areas (Stirling City, Inskip), so hour and place are confounded

phone_alert_reach_by_hour.behaviour: Share of households a CodeRED-style call reaches, by local hour
phone_alert_reach_by_hour.label: derived
phone_alert_reach_by_hour.transferability: low: person-level bound applied per household; hour effect confounded with place

self_initiated_kincade.behaviour: Evacuees by trigger, Kincade GPS: self before any notice / shadow outside zones / on warning / on order
self_initiated_kincade.derivation: share of in-zone evacuees who left before any notice = 0.33 / (0.33 + 0.07 + 0.38) = 0.423
self_initiated_kincade.label: derived
self_initiated_kincade.transferability: medium: GPS (not survey); Kincade residents had lived through Tubbs 2017; slow-moving fire with days of warning. Kincade survey: 22 of 270 commenters left before or without an order (Kuligowski 2022 p. 17)

camp_delay_mean.derivation: 09:33 - 08:00 = 93 min, a difference of two sample means
camp_delay_mean.label: derived
camp_delay_mean.transferability: high for Camp; no percentiles published (only Fig. 3, p. 38)

marshall_delay_moments.population: Marshall 2021 evacuees, N=129 in the regression
marshall_delay_moments.label: sourced
marshall_delay_moments.transferability: medium: Colorado suburban grass fire, daytime, 100 mph winds; the coefficient of variation (1.93) is the only published spread for a wildfire delay

departure_delay_lognormal.behaviour: Delay from trigger to departure, lognormal
departure_delay_lognormal.derivation: sigma from Marshall's coefficient of variation: sigma = sqrt(ln(1 + (263.44/136.59)^2)) = 1.246; median from the Camp mean: 93 / exp(1.246^2 / 2) = 42.8 min. Uncapped p10/p50/p90 = 8.6/42.8/213 min. Capped at 1440 min (assumption: one day).
departure_delay_lognormal.label: derived
departure_delay_lognormal.transferability: medium: Camp level, Marshall shape (two events joined; neither publishes Camp's spread)

delay_by_first_source_camp.behaviour: Change in preparation time by first source of awareness (ref: call, text, online, TV, radio)
delay_by_first_source_camp.locator: Table 3, p. 46; text p. 53 (notice p = 0.099; others not significant; order +47.1 p < 0.01, attributed to orders arriving after departure had begun)
delay_by_first_source_camp.label: sourced
delay_by_first_source_camp.transferability: low: not significant except the order effect, which is reverse-causal. Not used: the model draws one delay distribution for every source

delay_by_awareness_time.behaviour: Later awareness, shorter gap (within an event)
delay_by_awareness_time.locator: Grajdura Table 3 p. 46; Forrister Table 7 p. 9
delay_by_awareness_time.label: sourced
delay_by_awareness_time.transferability: low as a clock-hour effect: it reflects urgency as the fire nears, which the twin's fire cue already carries. Not used

departure_hour_wong.locator: Table 6, p. 17 of the pre-print; hour shares in wong2020 Table 10 p. 37
departure_hour_wong.label: sourced
departure_hour_wong.transferability: context only: the hour of departure, not a delay by hour

sought_information_wong.behaviour: Order recipients who sought more information (mandatory / voluntary order)
sought_information_wong.label: sourced

trips_before_evacuating_wong.behaviour: Evacuees who made one or more trips before evacuating ('to collect household members or find supplies'; purposes not asked)
trips_before_evacuating_wong.label: derived

trip_purpose_marshall.behaviour: Purposes of trips made before evacuating (table shares sum to 100)
trip_purpose_marshall.locator: QR 349 Table 1. The report text gives 22/25/18/13% for the same items; the table is used
trip_purpose_marshall.label: sourced

pickup_toward_fire.behaviour: Drives toward the fire to pick up family
pickup_toward_fire.note: No count anywhere. NIST TN 2252 p. 65 names parents possibly going back to Ponderosa Elementary on Pentz Road; p. 73 calls intermediate trips beyond scope. The model draws family trips (trip_purpose_marshall) but not their direction.
pickup_toward_fire.label: gap

return_during_closure.behaviour: Evacuees who went back into a closed or burning zone
return_during_closure.label: gap

gps_route_wong.behaviour: Evacuees who used GPS and followed its route / used it but rarely followed / did not use
gps_route_wong.locator: Table 10, p. 37 (78.2% or more had navigation available, Table A1 p. 61)
gps_route_wong.label: sourced

route_reason.behaviour: Familiar route vs following other cars
route_reason.note: No survey share found for Camp, Wong, Kincade or Marshall. Camp interviews: 'simply trying to escape the fire than having a specific route in mind' (Grajdura p. 112). The split of non-GPS drivers is an assumption that reuses BehaviorParams.herding_prob (0.3).
route_reason.label: gap

congestion_response.behaviour: Leaving the route because of congestion
congestion_response.label: sourced
congestion_response.transferability: low: qualitative counts, not a rate

camp_vehicle_abandonment.behaviour: Vehicles abandoned on Camp egress roads
camp_vehicle_abandonment.label: sourced

destination_marshall.label: sourced
destination_marshall.transferability: medium; corroborates Wong (friends or family about half, hotels about a fifth, shelters under a tenth)

pets_share.locator: Wong Table A1 p. 61; Kuligowski 2022 p. 7; TN 2103 PDF p. 16; Forrister Table 4 p. 8
pets_share.label: sourced

vehicles_wong.behaviour: Personal vehicles used to evacuate: one / two / more than two
vehicles_wong.label: sourced
vehicles_wong.transferability: high (California). Marshall: one 52.25%, two or more 30.32% (QR 349 Table 1)

persons_per_vehicle.derivation: Camp household size mean ~2.37 (Grajdura Table 1 p. 36: 1 23.4%, 2 36.2%, 3 20.2%, 4+ 20.2%, 4+ counted as 4) / 1.72 vehicles per evacuating household (Wong Oct 2017, >2 counted as 3) = 1.38; two different samples, so weak
persons_per_vehicle.label: derived
persons_per_vehicle.transferability: low: no survey measures it. Not drawn per household; reported for context

needs_assistance_kincade.behaviour: Survey commenters who said they needed assistance to evacuate
needs_assistance_kincade.label: sourced
needs_assistance_kincade.transferability: low: open comments, not a question; a household-level 'needs help to leave' share is not published

disability_households.behaviour: Households with a member with a disability / a medical condition
disability_households.locator: Wong Table A1 p. 61; Forrister Table 4 p. 8
disability_households.label: sourced
disability_households.transferability: medium: an upper bound on needing help to evacuate

camp_assistance_events.behaviour: Camp entrapment, assistance and rescue events
camp_assistance_events.label: sourced
camp_assistance_events.transferability: high for Camp (outcome check; NIST says the record is a fraction of events)

no_vehicle_acs.label: sourced
no_vehicle_acs.transferability: high (per-zone ACS is used when the twin has it)

help_request_share.behaviour: Share of no-vehicle or assistance-needing households that ask for help
help_request_share.note: Not found. Grajdura p. 74: at least 7% of Camp respondents needed a stranger's or police vehicle or walked. The 0.5 in sim/gen_residents.py CARLESS_TRANSPORT_REQUEST_SHARE is an assumption and is kept.
help_request_share.label: gap

wait_and_see_field_mclennan2019.behaviour: Residents who, before the fire, intended to wait and see; and what they did
wait_and_see_field_mclennan2019.population: eight Australian field-interview studies, 23 fires, n=1,641 threatened residents (unweighted means)
wait_and_see_field_mclennan2019.derivation: share of order-compliant households that wait for the fire cue = (0.17 x 2/3) / 0.875 = 0.13 (wait-and-see residents who eventually left, over the California compliance share)
wait_and_see_field_mclennan2019.label: derived
wait_and_see_field_mclennan2019.transferability: low to medium: actual threatened residents (better than the hypothetical 29%), but under the Australian stay-or-go policy

return_attempts_mclennan2019.behaviour: Residents away from home when warned who tried to return before the fire arrived
return_attempts_mclennan2019.reasons: defend the property, final preparations, livestock or pets, valuables
return_attempts_mclennan2019.locator: author preprint p. 18 (NSW online survey n=589; Perth Hills interviews n=91)
return_attempts_mclennan2019.label: sourced
return_attempts_mclennan2019.transferability: medium: people away from home mostly go back; the model does not track who is away

black_summer_response.locator: p. 12 (response), p. 31 (first awareness); 45% of the tourists who travelled toward a burning area did so to defend property or help family (pp. 12, 69)
black_summer_response.label: sourced
black_summer_response.transferability: low for California: defending is policy-endorsed in Australia (43% stayed to defend vs 4% sheltered)

black_saturday_late_leaving.behaviour: Black Saturday 2009: stayed to defend / sheltered / left; lateness among leavers
black_saturday_late_leaving.locator: author preprint pp. 17-18, quoting Whittaker et al. 2013 (IJWF 22:841-849) p. 845; mail survey n=1,314. Secondary quote: Whittaker 2013 itself not read
black_saturday_late_leaving.label: sourced

fort_mcmurray_prep_time.behaviour: Time spent getting ready to leave
fort_mcmurray_prep_time.population: Fort McMurray 2016, n=447 (shares sum to 0.929 as published)
fort_mcmurray_prep_time.label: sourced
fort_mcmurray_prep_time.transferability: medium: a cross-check of departure_delay only (preparation time, not awareness to departure)
fort_mcmurray_prep_time.cross_check: normalised over the 0.929 who answered: <15 min 0.308, 15-60 min 0.421, 1-2 h 0.179, >2 h 0.093; the grounded delay lognormal gives 0.200, 0.407, 0.189, 0.204 (see docs/people-data.md, Cross-check)

fort_mcmurray_awareness.behaviour: How Fort McMurray residents became aware they had to leave
fort_mcmurray_awareness.label: sourced
fort_mcmurray_awareness.transferability: medium (single-order urban evacuation of 88,000 people); not used

self_evacuation_archetypes.behaviour: Self-evacuation archetypes (decision types, not observed behaviour)
self_evacuation_archetypes.label: sourced
self_evacuation_archetypes.transferability: low (Australia; a typology, not rates); not used

kincade_delay_after_order_gps.behaviour: Delay of departure after the order or warning for the person's zone (0 if they left before it), median per block group
kincade_delay_after_order_gps.label: sourced
kincade_delay_after_order_gps.transferability: medium: the only delay measured from the order itself; slow fire with days of notice and night orders. Not drawn (block-group medians, not a household distribution)

legacy.description: Reproduces the model before this file: everyone is told and leaves, 30 min lognormal delay (TrafficParams), no trips, routes from the twin, no pets.

route_strategy.label: legacy
route_strategy.note: the fixed-delay twin routes every packet by the fastest route

destination_type.label: legacy
destination_type.note: the twin sends vehicles to exits, not destination types

grounded.description: Camp-like no-notice fire: Camp values where they exist, else other California fires (Wong 2020, Kincade), else other US fires, else a labelled assumption.

order_compliance.label: sourced
order_compliance.note: Oct 2017 N. California, as PEOPLE_PRESETS camp_2018_sourced

stay_mode.label: derived
stay_mode.note: defend = Gatlinburg stayers citing property (30.2%, inside Wong's 16.7-36.7%); every other stayer shelters at home. Reasons are select-all, so this treats the property reason as the deciding one

wait_and_see_given_compliance.label: derived
wait_and_see_given_compliance.note: (0.17 x 2/3) / 0.875; low transferability (Australia). Sensitivity: 0.07 (BehaviorParams.wait_for_fire_share) to 0.33 (McLennan 2014 hypothetical)

milling.label: sourced
milling.note: Oct 2017 N. California mandatory-order recipients who sought more information. Time spent is inside departure_delay (not drawn separately)

route_strategy.label: assumption
route_strategy.note: navigation 0.189 is sourced (Wong Oct 2017 used GPS and followed it); the rest is split 0.7 familiar / 0.3 follow others by the herding_prob assumption

reroutes_in_congestion.label: assumption
reroutes_in_congestion.note: no rate published; Kincade comments show some took back roads

destination_type.label: sourced
destination_type.note: Wong Oct 2017 N. California; hotel includes Airbnb (2.7%)

vehicles_taken.label: sourced
vehicles_taken.note: Oct 2017 N. California; 'more than two' drawn as 3; rental/other modes (2.8%) dropped

needs_assistance.label: derived
needs_assistance.note: 15/192 Kincade commenters; below the 14-19% of households with a disability, which is an upper bound
